title: Geo-anchor routing and automated evidence pipeline for hosted API residency
creator: Aisha Ndlovu
description: Goal: Provide a tenant-facing geo-anchor (region affinity) routing control for the Hosted API plus an evidence-generation pipeline that produces auditable residency and retention proofs automatically. Scope: (1) new tenant setting 'Geo‑Anchor' with UI and API to pin preferred region(s) and optional hard-lock; (2) routing policy enforcement in request gateway with soft/hard semantics and capacity-aware fallbacks; (3) retention policy configuration for short/medium/long retention windows per tenant; (4) evidence exporter that bundles residency metadata (request routing logs, model variant metadata, retention TTLs) into signed daily reports for compliance teams and customers; (5) UX in Console for policy status, recent evidence bundles, and automated attestations for SOC/GDPR-style audits. Out of scope for this ticket: non-hosted Private deployments and per-request content classification for residency. This ticket coordinates PM acceptance, design mocks, engineering work, security review, and an initial canary rollout to a set of compliant customers.
acceptance_criteria: Console: Tenant can set Geo-Anchor to one or more regions and choose soft (prefer) or hard (strict) enforcement
API: Admin API endpoints support setting geo_anchor, enforcement_mode, and retention_tier; changes are auditable
Routing: Gateway respects Geo-Anchor with documented fallback order and logs routing decisions to residency log stream
Retention: Tenant retention tiers map to retention TTLs and are reflected in evidence bundles
Evidence: Daily signed evidence bundle generated to S3-compatible storage with checksum and manifest; bundle includes tenant_id, routing decisions, timestamps, model_variant_ids, and retention_config
Security: Evidence bundles are encrypted at rest and access-controlled; security review completed and documented
Metrics: Dashboard shows % of requests honoring geo-anchor, fallback counts, and evidence generation success rate
Rollout: Canary plan executed against 5 pilot tenants with no customer-impact incidents
tasks: PM: finalize policy semantics doc and acceptance criteria (this ticket)
Design: deliver Console flows for geo-anchor modal, retention selector, and evidence download page
Eng-Gateway: implement enforcement flags and residency log emissions to kafka-residency topic
Eng-Runtime: annotate model_variant metadata and surface region compatibility
Eng-Backend: admin APIs, tenant config persistence, and evidence bundle assembler service
Eng-Infra: S3 bucket + KMS policy for evidence storage and lifecycle rules
Security: run threat model for evidence pipeline and approve KMS/HSM usage
QA: synthetic tests for routing, fallback, and end-to-end evidence bundle integrity
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Canary): deploy feature flags to staging and enable for 5 pilot tenants - observe routing and evidence bundles for 7 days
Phase 1 (Beta): open to self-serve tenants behind consent toggle; monitor dashboard metrics and manual audits
Phase 2 (GA): enable default soft-mode for new tenants; provide hard-lock via contract amendment and SRM approval
Rollback: toggle enforcement_mode to 'prefer' globally and ship compensation job to reclassify any misrouted requests in evidence bundles
notes: Trade-offs: hard-lock guarantees residency but reduces available capacity and increases latency/fallback risk; soft-mode favors availability and cost efficiency.
Decision 2026-02-27: prefer soft-mode default to avoid immediate capacity cliffs; require sales/legal sign-off to enable hard-lock for a tenant.
Performance: gateway-level checks must be cheap (~sub-ms) and rely on precomputed tenant-region affinity table refreshed every 30s.
Privacy: evidence bundles must avoid including customer content; only metadata (timestamps, model IDs, hashes) will be included per legal guidance.
Future: consider per-request residency tags and per-model regional pinning as follow-up (tracked separately).
